newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares encouraged by strong Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: German shares encouraged by strong Wall Street.

text.p: The German IBIS DAX index ended afternoon electronic dealings on Monday just above the psychologically important level of 2,700 points, lifted by strength on Wall Street.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings in the DAX index of 30 blue-chip stocks, ended up 8.14 points, or 0.3 percent, at 2,700.83, after the Dow Jones surged in its early dealings.
The DAX index had ended floor trade up 7.85 points, or 0.29 percent, at 2,693.88.
Early last week the DAX index reached record highs above the level of 2,700, but then fell back somewhat. Analysts had widely anticipated that it would test the level again.
Although Wall Street was supportive, the dollar slipped back to trade at 1.5290 marks which put pressure on export-oriented German stocks.

During the session on Monday the chemicals sector was a favourite, dealers said, with Bayer AG ending electronic trade up 30 pfennigs at 58.44, BASF AG up 35 pfennigs at 49.75 and Hoechst AG gaining 21 pfennigs to stand at 58.60.
Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, in the spotlight since last week on talk that Deutsche Bank AG has upped its ownership in the Bavarian bank, ended IBIS up 47 pfennigs at 55.72.
Electronic giant Siemens recovered earlier losses to end computer trade up nine pfennigs at 80.56 marks, after the Dutch electronics group Philips issued a surprise profit warning.

Amongst the medium-sized firms, engineering company Deutsche Babcock AG ended nearly fourteen percent lower in IBIS dealings, falling 7.50 marks to 46.50 after it said it would incur a higher charge for its restructuring measures than originally expected.

New stock Fresenius Medical Care AG continued to bloom on the MDAX index of medium-sized companies, rising six marks to end IBIS dealings at 121.45, with dealers saying interest was coming from the U.S..

Meanwhile lead creditor Deutsche Bank of Traub AG sought the suspension of the engineering company's stock. The firm said it faced serious liqidity problems and its creditors would meet later on Monday.
Dealers said Deutsche Bank's own loss during the day was bound up with the difficulties at Traub. The bank slipped 49 pfennigs to end the day at 71.68 marks.
